title: 3891. Minimum Increase to Maximize Special Indices

examples.explanation: Start with nums = [1, 2, 2]. Increase nums[1] by 1, array becomes [1, 3, 2]. The final array is [1, 3, 2] has 1 special index, which is the maximum achievable. It is impossible to achieve this number of special indices with fewer operations. Thus, the answer is 1.

Start with nums = [2, 1, 1, 3]. Perform 2 operations at index 1, array becomes [2, 3, 1, 3]. The final array is [2, 3, 1, 3] has 1 special index, which is the maximum achievable. Thus, the answer is 2.

Start with nums = [5, 2, 1, 4, 3]. Perform 4 operations at index 1, array becomes [5, 6, 1, 4, 3]. The final array is [5, 6, 1, 4, 3] has 2 special indices, which is the maximum achievable. Thus, the answer is 4.
